#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fetch abugoshfestival.co.il's programme for one edition into its raw folder.

Run it by hand, on a machine that can reach the site. It never runs on a schedule:

    python3 scraper/festivals/abu_gosh/sources/abugosh-site/fetch.py --edition 2026

It writes `data/festivals/abu-gosh/<edition>/abugosh-site/` (`programme.json` and
`manifest.json`) and nothing else. The records keep the site's own vocabulary:
its WordPress post ids, its card labels ("Church Concert No. 1"), its place
names and its prices in shekels.

Pages read: the English Concert Schedule (every ticketed concert, Tel Aviv
Museum, Kiryat Ye'arim Church and the Crypt alike) and Outdoor Performances
(the free courtyard sets); their Hebrew twins, for Hebrew titles, paired by
URL slug; and each card's own English page, for the price, the Smarticket
link, the running time and the description. Each card's picture is the
listing card's own.

Two things refuse the write. First, the year the schedule's heading prints
("Concerts Board 2026", and the Hebrew "לוח קונצרטים 2026") must equal the
edition id: the festival runs twice a year (Shavuot and Sukkot), so the id
alone says nothing about which of the two the site shows, but a site rolled
over to next year cannot pass. Second, every performance must fall inside the
edition's declared dates (`common.guard_dates`), which is what tells this
year's Sukkot programme from its Shavuot one.

The parsing half lives in parse.py and is proven offline by its self-test.
"""

import os
import sys
import urllib.parse

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))))
import common
import parse as aparse
import registry

FESTIVAL_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
SOURCE_ID = "abugosh-site"
# Bumped when the shape of programme.json changes.
FETCHER_VERSION = 1

SITE = "https://abugoshfestival.co.il"
SCHEDULE = urllib.parse.quote("/לוח-קונצרטים/")
OUTDOOR = "/outside/"
# Which listing a card came from, and its English and Hebrew pages.
LISTINGS = [
    ("concerts", SITE + "/en" + SCHEDULE, SITE + SCHEDULE),
    ("outdoor", SITE + "/en" + OUTDOOR, SITE + OUTDOOR),
]


def _url(href):
    """A card link as the site prints it (Hebrew path segments raw) -> a fetchable URL."""
    return urllib.parse.quote(href, safe=":/%?=&")


def build(edition, cache_dir):
    year = int(edition["id"])
    cards = []
    for listing, en_url, he_url in LISTINGS:
        en = common.cached_page(cache_dir, en_url)
        he = common.cached_page(cache_dir, he_url)
        if en is None or he is None:
            raise common.FetchRefused("%s: the listing page is gone (404) — nothing written" % listing)
        if listing == "concerts":
            for where, page in ((en_url, en), (he_url, he)):
                found = aparse.year_marker(page)
                if found != year:
                    raise common.FetchRefused(
                        "%s says programme year %r, edition %s was asked for. The site may now be "
                        "serving another edition, so nothing was written" % (where, found, edition["id"]))
        hebrew = {c["slug"]: c for c in aparse.parse_listing(he)}
        for card in aparse.parse_listing(en):
            twin = hebrew.get(card["slug"])
            card["listing"] = listing
            card["date"] = aparse.iso_date(card["dayMonth"], year)
            card["titleHe"] = twin["title"] if twin else None
            card["placeHe"] = twin["place"] if twin else None
            cards.append(card)
    if not cards:
        raise common.FetchRefused("no programme cards on the listing pages — nothing written")
    common.guard_dates(edition, [c["date"] for c in cards])

    details = common.fetch_all(lambda c: common.cached_page(cache_dir, _url(c["url"])), cards)
    for card, page in zip(cards, details):
        card["detail"] = aparse.parse_detail(page) if page else None
    cards.sort(key=lambda c: (c["date"], c["times"][0]["start"] if c["times"] else "", c["postId"]))
    return {"site": SITE, "year": year, "cards": cards}


def main():
    args = common.parse_args(__doc__)
    festival = registry.load(FESTIVAL_DIR)
    edition = registry.edition(festival, args.edition)
    programme = build(edition, registry.cache_dir(festival, edition["id"], SOURCE_ID))
    common.write_raw(
        festival,
        edition["id"],
        SOURCE_ID,
        {"programme.json": programme},

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fetch abugoshfestival.co.il's programme for one edition into its raw folder.

Run it by hand, on a machine that can reach the site. It never runs on a schedule:

    python3 scraper/festivals/abu_gosh/sources/abugosh-site/fetch.py --edition 2026

It writes `data/festivals/abu-gosh/<edition>/abugosh-site/` (`programme.json` and
`manifest.json`) and nothing else. The records keep the site's own vocabulary:
its WordPress post ids, its card labels ("Church Concert No. 1"), its place
names and its prices in shekels.

Pages read: the English Concert Schedule (every ticketed concert, Tel Aviv
Museum, Kiryat Ye'arim Church and the Crypt alike) and Outdoor Performances
(the free courtyard sets); their Hebrew twins, for Hebrew titles, paired by
URL slug; and each card's own English page, for the price, the Smarticket
link, the running time and the description. Each card's picture is the
listing card's own.

Two things refuse the write. First, the year the schedule's heading prints
("Concerts Board 2026", and the Hebrew "לוח קונצרטים 2026") must equal the
edition id: the festival runs twice a year (Shavuot and Sukkot), so the id
alone says nothing about which of the two the site shows, but a site rolled
over to next year cannot pass. Second, every performance must fall inside the
edition's declared dates (`common.guard_dates`), which is what tells this
year's Sukkot programme from its Shavuot one.

The parsing half lives in parse.py and is proven offline by its self-test.
"""

import os
import sys
import urllib.parse

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))))
import common
import parse as aparse
import registry

FESTIVAL_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
SOURCE_ID = "abugosh-site"
# Bumped when the shape of programme.json changes.
FETCHER_VERSION = 1

SITE = "https://abugoshfestival.co.il"
SCHEDULE = urllib.parse.quote("/לוח-קונצרטים/")
OUTDOOR = "/outside/"
# Which listing a card came from, and its English and Hebrew pages.
LISTINGS = [
    ("concerts", SITE + "/en" + SCHEDULE, SITE + SCHEDULE),
    ("outdoor", SITE + "/en" + OUTDOOR, SITE + OUTDOOR),
]


def _url(href):
    """A card link as the site prints it (Hebrew path segments raw) -> a fetchable URL."""
    return urllib.parse.quote(href, safe=":/%?=&")


def build(edition, cache_dir):
    year = int(edition["id"])
    cards = []
    for listing, en_url, he_url in LISTINGS:
        en = common.cached_page(cache_dir, en_url)
        he = common.cached_page(cache_dir, he_url)
        if en is None or he is None:
            raise common.FetchRefused("%s: the listing page is gone (404) — nothing written" % listing)
        if listing == "concerts":
            for where, page in ((en_url, en), (he_url, he)):
                found = aparse.year_marker(page)
                if found != year:
                    raise common.FetchRefused(
                        "%s says programme year %r, edition %s was asked for. The site may now be "
                        "serving another edition, so nothing was written" % (where, found, edition["id"]))
        hebrew = {c["slug"]: c for c in aparse.parse_listing(he)}
        for card in aparse.parse_listing(en):
            twin = hebrew.get(card["slug"])
            card["listing"] = listing
            card["date"] = aparse.iso_date(card["dayMonth"], year)
            card["titleHe"] = twin["title"] if twin else None
            card["placeHe"] = twin["place"] if twin else None
            cards.append(card)
    if not cards:
        raise common.FetchRefused("no programme cards on the listing pages — nothing written")
    common.guard_dates(edition, [c["date"] for c in cards])

    details = common.fetch_all(lambda c: common.cached_page(cache_dir, _url(c["url"])), cards)
    for card, page in zip(cards, details):
        card["detail"] = aparse.parse_detail(page) if page else None
    cards.sort(key=lambda c: (c["date"], c["times"][0]["start"] if c["times"] else "", c["postId"]))
    return {"site": SITE, "year": year, "cards": cards}


def main():
    args = common.parse_args(__doc__)
    festival = registry.load(FESTIVAL_DIR)
    edition = registry.edition(festival, args.edition)
    programme = build(edition, registry.cache_dir(festival, edition["id"], SOURCE_ID))
    common.write_raw(
        festival,
        edition["id"],
        SOURCE_ID,
        {"programme.json": programme},
        fetcher="scraper/festivals/abu_gosh/sources/abugosh-site/fetch.py",
        fetcher_version=FETCHER_VERSION,
        urls=[url for _, en, he in LISTINGS for url in (en, he)] + [SITE + "/en/<listing>/<card slug>/"],
        notes="The English Concert Schedule and Outdoor Performances pages give every card "
              "(post id, picture, label, day/month, times, place, title, blurb); their Hebrew "
              "twins give Hebrew titles and places by URL slug; each card's own page gives the "
              "price, Smarticket link, running time and description (parse.py). The year is the "
              "schedule heading's, checked against the edition id.",
    )
    print("%d cards (%d with a price, %d free)" % (
        len(programme["cards"]),
        sum(1 for c in programme["cards"] if c["detail"] and c["detail"]["price"] is not None),
        sum(1 for c in programme["cards"] if c["detail"] and c["detail"]["free"]),
    ))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

- **A landed commit is revised by a new commit**, never a rewrite of that one.

  else was in progress.

I added the Abu Gosh Music Festival, Sukkot 2026 edition, and committed it. `npm run verify` passes. The festival has 27 events and 34 performances across 3 venues, and every event has a picture.

**Branch:** `worktree-agent-adddeb0ff409ad368`
**Commit:** `c2349fa` "Add Abu Gosh Music Festival 2026 programme" (not pushed, no PR)

**What's in it**
- **Dates:** The edition runs 29 Sep – 3 Oct 2026. I started it on 29 Sep, not 30 Sep, because the Tel Aviv concerts are part of this same edition. The site's "Concert Schedule" page lists all 17 ticketed concerts on one page: 4 at the Tel Aviv Museum on 29/9, 9 at Kiryat Ye'arim Church and 4 in the Crypt. The Abu Gosh page alone has 13, not the 14 the prompt mentioned.
- **Outdoor performances:** I also included the "Outdoor Performances" page. These are 12 free sets in the church courtyard, some playing several times a day. They are served as free (price 0). "Coffee, Jazz & Israeli Song" has three pages, one per day, so it is merged into one event with 7 performances.
- **Images:** Every event's picture comes from its listing card.
- **Hebrew titles:** Each event carries its Hebrew title, matched to the English card by the page address the two sites share.
- **Prices and tickets:** Each concert's price comes from its own page (120–230 NIS) and is set as that performance's min and max price. Each concert also carries its Smarticket ticket link, running time (null for St John Passion, whose page gives none) and full description.
- **Categories:** They follow the site's own menu: Tel Aviv, Abu Gosh, Crypt, Outdoor.
- **Availability:** Ticketed concerts show "unknown" because the site says nothing about seats left. The free sets show "free".
- **Venues:** Each has cited coordinates.
  - Kiryat Ye'arim Church uses the festival's own Waze pin. The Café Terrace and the Patio are rooms of it, marked outdoor.
  - The Crypt uses the Benedictine monastery's pin from Wikipedia.
  - Tel Aviv Museum of Art uses its Wikipedia pin and the address 27 Shaul HaMelech Blvd.
  - Capacity, layout and accessibility are null.
- **festival.toml:** id `abu-gosh`, folder `abu_gosh`, kind `music`, `subtypes = ["music-classical", "music-vocal"]`. The `[ticketing]` section has `model = "central-box-office"`, `url = "https://agfestival.smarticket.co.il/"`, a note and currency ILS.
- **Year guard:** The fetcher refuses to write unless the schedule's heading year ("Concerts Board 2026" / "לוח קונצרטים 2026") matches the edition. The date check then tells this Sukkot programme apart from the Shavuot one. The "Shavuot 2026" wording in the Abu Gosh page's intro is old text; the schedule itself is Sukkot.

**Files**
- `scraper/festivals/abu_gosh/festival.toml`
- `scraper/festivals/abu_gosh/sources/abugosh-site/{fetch.py, parse.py}`. The parser has a `--selftest` that runs on 6 real captured pages in `samples/`, stripped of scripts and styles (about 85–170 KB each).
- `scraper/festivals/abu_gosh/curated/venues.json`
- `scraper/convert/adapters/abu_gosh/{abugosh_site.py, venues_research.py}`
- `data/festivals/abu-gosh/2026/abugosh-site/{programme.json, manifest.json}`
- `site/data/festivals/abu-gosh/2026.json` and `site/data/festivals/index.json`
- The generator-output allowlist, with 3 entries added.

**Worth checking**
- **Festival name:** I used the site's own "Abu Gosh Music Festival". Wikipedia calls it the Abu Ghosh Vocal Music Festival.
- **Edition id:** It is just "2026" (the registry only takes a year). The festival also runs at Shavuot, so a Shavuot edition could not have its own id under the current rules.
- **Patio location:** The site places the Patio only at the church grounds in general. The venue notes say so.
- **Clashing listing:** On 1/10, the Café Terrace has Getride's Quintet at 16:15 while "Coffee, Jazz" is listed in the same slot. That is the site's own listing; I kept both as given.
- **Hebrew-only difference:** Buxtehude's Hebrew title on the site differs in meaning from the English one.
- **UI tests:** I did not run `npm run test:ui`. The only change under `site/` is data, and the requirements harness uses its own frozen copy of the festival index.

The Tel Aviv Festival 2026 is added and committed on branch `worktree-agent-a19736199ad37c4a6`, commit `e68d14b` (not pushed). `npm run verify` passes. `npm run test:ui` fails 3 planNG cases, but those can't be caused by this change (details under "Open points").

**Counts:** 54 events, 69 performances and 5 venues, from 59 shows and 6 programme days.
- The 59 show records become 54 events because records with the same name are grouped into one event: Dunietz, Tzitrin, Ben Tzur, Castel-Bloom and CIAM each appear twice.
- 39 of the 54 events have an image. Each image is the show's `photo` from the programme page, made into an absolute URL.
- Every show also has its own `/show/<id>` page. I checked a few: they repeat the same record, and a show with no photo only gets the generic `brand/og.png`. So the 15 events without an image have no picture anywhere on the site, and I fetch only `/program`.

**Files** (under `/home/user/EdFringeNow/.claude/worktrees/agent-a19736199ad37c4a6/`):
- `scraper/festivals/tel_aviv_festival/`:
  - `festival.toml`: id `tel-aviv-festival`, served in Hebrew right-to-left, kind `multi`, subtypes `["music-israeli","art-museum"]`, ordinal 2 (the site says it is back "for the second time"), 1–8 Nov.
  - `[ticketing]` has pass price 159, `model = "festival-pass"` and `url = "https://telavivfestival.co.il/#tickets"`, as the coordinator asked.
- `sources/festival-site/fetch.py` and `parse.py`: `parse.py` is pure and has `--selftest`; its sample `samples/program.html` is the real page fetched on 27 Sep.
  - It joins the pushed payload strings and decodes the `days`, `shows` and `settings` values.
  - Year check: the year comes from the page title ("פסטיבל תל־אביב 2026"). Each day's printed weekday (`dow`) must fall on its "1.11"-style date in that year, or the fetch is refused. The selftest proves a 2027 page would be refused.
- `curated/venues.json`: every figure has a source URL, and coordinates also say what they are based on.
  - Venues: Tel Aviv Museum of Art (12 rooms, including the sculpture garden and three exhibitions a show plays inside), Beit Ariela (auditorium and urban salon), TAPAC, Heichal HaTarbut (אולם לאוי), Beit Radical.
  - Addresses and coordinates come from Wikipedia (English and Hebrew) and from radical.org.il/contact, which gives a Google Maps pin.
  - All capacities are null.
- Adapters in `scraper/convert/adapters/tel_aviv_festival/`:
  - `festival_site.py`: its docstring explains the event grouping, categories, genres, statuses, ticket links and prices.
  - `venues_research.py`: turns the curated file into served venues.
- Also committed: the raw files in `data/festivals/tel-aviv-festival/2026/festival-site/`, the served file `site/data/festivals/tel-aviv-festival/2026.json`, `index.json`, and the new entries in the generator-output allowlist.

**Decisions to check:**
- **Prices.**
  - Night Pass shows: 159, the price of that evening's pass. That covers the whole evening, not one show.
  - Hall add-ons: 159 + `addonPrice`. They are only sold as one combined pass-plus-show ticket; the Ticketmaster page "פס רביעי + שימי תבורי" shows 209 = 159 + 50.
  - Separately sold shows: their printed `price` (139, 149 or 209).
  - Free shows: 0.
  - Opening and closing: price unknown (null), since the site prints none.
- **Sold out.** The source includes availability, so `soldout` becomes sold-out (one performance, CIAM on the 22:15 Thursday slot).
- **After midnight.** Shows listed at 00:00 or 00:30 are served as 24:00 or 24:30 on that night's date, following the convention in `schema.py`.
- **Categories.** Opening, the Friday noon block, the after party, closing, and the two museum nights together as "פס ערב במוזיאון תל־אביב לאמנות".
- **Genres.** Music by default, with exceptions by show id:
  - film: the two midnight screenings
  - dance: Inbal Pinto's piece
  - talk: the master class, the two live podcasts, and the curator's talk
  - "30 שנה לקלרה הקדושה" stays music, because the soundtrack is played live.

**Open points:**
- **test:ui failures.** The 3 failing cases are `planng-photo-fade.23.18`, `planng-arrival.24.7` and `planng-verdict-tip.20.17`. Only `planng-arrival` failed again when I re-ran those three. The test harness serves festival data from its frozen fixtures, not from `site/data`, so this change can't be the cause. It looks like it was already failing, or depends on the environment.
- **No city photo.** planNG has no Tel Aviv picture in `site/planNG/cities/`; that is outside this task.
- **My mistake.** On one set of Wikipedia page fetches, I put the owner's email in the User-Agent header. That broke the rule against sending it to unrelated services, and I didn't repeat it.

ISRA 2026 is added and committed but not pushed. Branch `worktree-agent-a26e37920c0cd6be2`, commit `d91cebb` ("Add ISRA Annual Conference 2026 programme"). `npm run verify` passes. `npm run test:ui` passed 205/205 on the second run. On the first run one animation-timing case (`planng-photo-fade.23.18`, opacity 0.0008 where 0 was expected) failed; it doesn't read the new data and passed on the rerun.

**Counts:** 26 events, 26 performances (one per session), 1 venue with 3 rooms. 12 of the 26 events have an image.

**What was built**
- **Festival:** id `isra`, folder `scraper/festivals/isra/`. `kind = "multi"`, with a comment saying it becomes "academic" once PR #917 lands. `subtypes = ["academic-radiology", "academic-medicine"]`, `default_genre = "talk"`, `lang = "en"`. The edition is 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-20 with no ordinal, because the site never numbers the conference. I left out a Hebrew name because the site doesn't publish one.
- **Source `eventact-agenda`:**
  - `fetch.py` reads the event id, agenda id and API token from the `<ea-program>` tag on `/isra<edition>/ScientificVProgram`. It then fetches the timetable and each activity's `/session`, and refuses to write if the timetable answers for a different agenda.
  - `parse.py` checks every activity's day-first `date` against its table's month-first `date` and refuses on a mismatch; the per-table `startDate` is ignored. Its `--selftest` runs on committed real samples: the programme page, the full timetable and three session answers.
- **Talks:** the session endpoint returns lectures with presenting speakers and institutes, 157 lectures in all. Each event's blurb lists them as "HH:MM title — speaker (institute)", plus the session's own note (for example "held in Hebrew"). The `/Lecture` endpoint wasn't needed.
- **Images:** each event's image is the first real speaker portrait in the session, skipping EventAct's default placeholder picture. 14 events have no real portrait anywhere in their session, so their image is null. The only other image on the programme page is the site-wide banner (`Welcome.jpeg`), which I did not use as a fallback. Tell me if the owner wants the banner there instead of null.
- **What's kept and what's skipped:**
  - Kept: the 24 scientific sessions, plus two evening social events. "Mingling – Music, Wine and Friends" has genre `other`; "Stand-up Comedy" has genre `comedy`.
  - Skipped as logistics: 11 registration, coffee break and lunch slots.
  - Sessions with no lectures, "ISRA Annual Meeting" and "The Last Imager Standing", are kept.
- **Venue:** David's Harp Galilee Resort, Kfar Nahum (Capernaum), named on the conference site's Home and Accommodation pages. Coordinates 32.88043, 35.57356 come from the map pin on the hotel's contact page. Rooms are hall-a/b/c.
  - Hall and seat counts are null: the programme's Hall A/B/C don't map onto the hotel's own halls (Agam 475, Agam A and B 200 each, amphitheatre 700). The notes say so.
  - Sessions listed in one hall get that room; activities listed across all halls get no room.
- **Tickets:** `[ticketing]` has the regular-rate fee table in ILS (full-conference and per-day rates, by category and membership). It also has `model = "festival-pass"` and `url` set to the Registration page, as you asked. Performances have `free: false`, `ticketUrl` set to the Registration page, and null prices, since the site prints no price per session.
- **Allowlist:** the raw manifest and programme files and the serving file are added in `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/data-dir-is-generator-output.mjs`.

**Uncertain**
- The city is given as "Capernaum" (the hotel says Kfar Nahum), and the festival point is the hotel's pin.
- The early-rate prices (until 25 Sept) are only mentioned in the notes, not served as figures.

_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Tkg1DM8zUNirsvzt7nNoyo?thread=cmsg_01Tkg1DM8zUNirsvzt7nNoyoB3hyNmiT2rtaMRSgX3tSRg)_

Before: the festival calendar carries three Israeli festivals (Jerusalem comedy, Acco, Haifa film), all ending by 22 Oct.

After: it also carries five Israeli festivals with full per-session programmes, from 29 Sep to 12 Nov 2026:

| festival | dates | sessions | pictures |
|---|---|---|---|
| Abu Gosh Music Festival (Sukkot) | 29 Sep - 3 Oct | 17 concerts + free courtyard sets (34 performances) | every event |
| InDNegev, Mitzpe Gvulot | 15-17 Oct | 120 sets on five stages | none published |
| ISRA 2026 radiology conference, David's Harp resort, Kfar Nahum | 18-20 Oct | 26 sessions, each listing its talks and speakers | 12 of 26 (speaker portraits) |
| Tel Aviv Festival | 1-8 Nov | 69 performances of 54 shows | 39 of 54 |
| Jerusalem International Oud Festival | 5-12 Nov | 16 concerts | every event |

How: each festival is a new `scraper/festivals/<dir>/` with a hand-run fetcher, a pure `parse.py` with a self-test over committed real samples, curated venues (every figure cited) and adapters, converted by `to_serving.py`. Every change is additive. Each `festival.toml` also carries the `subtypes` list #917 introduces and the `[ticketing] model`/`url` #919 introduces; main ignores both until those land, and `index.json` is regenerated when this branch meets them. ISRA is `kind = "multi"` until #917 adds `academic`.

Per festival:
- **InDNegev**: the schedule page renders only Thursday; the whole timetable is a literal in one of its script chunks. The fetcher finds that chunk and applies the chunk's own display filter, so the talks area and the early Thursday Raket sets the site hides are skipped. Sets after midnight are dated by the calendar day they start on. One festival pass; no per-set price.
- **Oud Festival**: listing card + each concert's page (blurb, printed price 90-250 ILS, Bimot ticket link); Hebrew.
- **Abu Gosh**: the "Concert Schedule" page (Tel Aviv Museum, Kiryat Ye'arim Church, the Crypt) plus the free outdoor programme; per-concert prices from each page; Hebrew titles matched by shared page address.
- **Tel Aviv Festival**: the programme is in the page's RSC payload. Pass-night shows are priced at that night's pass (159), hall add-ons at pass + add-on (only sold combined), separate shows at their printed price, opening/closing unknown. One show marked sold out on the site is served sold-out.
- **ISRA**: the EventAct agenda API behind the programme page (timetable + per-session lectures). Registration, coffee and lunch slots are skipped; the two evening social events are kept.

Checks: `npm run verify` and `npm run test:ui` (205/205) pass locally; served in the planner, all five sit in the year strip and InDNegev plans.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- backfilling-provenance: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history. Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- changing-pack-elements: What a change to a pack's element owes - the entry on its provenance file, which kind, and how to append it - and what a pack's README carries. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md, skills, checks, tasks, manifest, README or provenance folder, in a repo's local pack or on a canon's shelf.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- data-pipeline: EdFringeNow's data pipeline - getting show data out of edfringe.com into the committed files the site serves, and the wire format the pages decode. Use before touching scraper/, data/, site/data/, the scrape and price tasks, or the site code that decodes, prices or times performances.
- deterministic-expecteds: What makes a rendered expected byte-stable — the pinned clock, faked inputs, real fonts, fixed-duration pumps — and the per-stack rendering recipe (jsdom+satori for DOM products, Flutter golden files) with pixel-exact comparison. Use when writing a case, the render harness or the fake world under dev/requirements.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked `task:origin:ad-hoc` and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- explore-link: Mine one given URL for product, market, usage and pricing insights and fold them into an existing product-wiki page — cited, dated, delivered as a PR. Use when the owner says "/explore-link <url>", or hands over a link and asks for it to be read into the wiki.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- extract-from-instructions: Convert instruction prose somebody already wrote into pack carriers, leaving the prose file a thin routing map. Use when adopting Claudinite on a repo that already carries a CLAUDE.md, when a person wants their machine-local instructions carried properly, or when asked to convert instruction prose into a pack.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve a repo's own comments as a pass of their own: delete, correct, add the why. Use when working a repo's comments deliberately (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner approves the current branch or PR, or asks to merge or land it into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production. Use when designing a larger element, when filing a migration plan's chain, when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- releasing-a-cloudflare-site: How a site served from Cloudflare is released — the version contract, the guards that stop a release loop or a half-release, forcing one, rolling one back, and which parts of Cloudflare only a person can change. Use when changing the release task, the wrangler config or the analytics loader, and when a release parks.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- requirements-harness: How EdFringeNow runs product/requirements.md as tests under a real headless Chromium - writing leaves and goldens, the harness's determinism traps, the frozen fixtures and golden approval. Use before editing product/requirements.md or anything under product/requirements/.
- revalidating-rules: Re-probe the pack rules whose truth lives outside the repository — harness tool contracts, token reach, whether an MCP tool exists, a platform's behaviour — and correct the ones that have gone stale. Use when a revalidation sweep runs over a corpus of packs, or when asked whether a rule's environmental claim still holds.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- triaging-usage-findings: Turn a usage-review finding that has lasted into a proposed change - read the element's provenance first, settle which of the rule's causes it is, and write the edit itself rather than a description of it. Use when a usage-triage run hands you lasting findings, or when an owner asks what to do about one.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a file a test or tool generates — naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, and resolving its merge conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- write-a-requirement-leaf: How a requirement leaf is written in the executable spec — the backtick-numbered one-liner with its detail collapsed under it, and which kind (surface snapshot, behavior, logic, saga, per-project, e2e singleton) its case takes. Use when adding or reshaping a requirement line in requirements.md.
- write-a-saga: How a saga case is written — a multi-step story captured as a golden storyboard or one animated APNG golden — steps, captions, frame budget, the real entry point, delay stripping and gesture marking. Use when authoring or changing a case under the saga kind.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: How a plan's phases are ordered so nothing stalls mid-run. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan (including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file), when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written - RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon - brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, the marker that names a rule's provenance file. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, and when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-repo-scanning-checks: How a check that scans the repo picks its file set, strips comments before matching a forbidden token, and proves itself silent against real sources. Loaded for any edit of a coded or declared check.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- writing-wiki-pages: How a product-wiki page is written and grown — the Key insights header, citation, what a source actually supports (attribution, independent voices, public proxies), correction without deletion, the growth log, sample-data, when a pass writes nothing. Loaded for any edit under product-wiki/.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
6. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

The merge leaves the local checkout on the branch it squashed, and no step here syncs `main`; the
merge is usually a session's last act. Only if you go on to start further work in this session,
sync first, before branching off anything:

```
git fetch origin main && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main && git remote prune origin
```
